paper.title_en: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
paper.abstract_en: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.
